BLOCKER: Python and Go validators disagree on strictness (`int("90")` accepted by Python; Go `json.Unmarshal` rejects it → cmd exits 2, `"egress": null` passes Python's key-presence check but is MISSING_GROUP in Go), and the gate maps any rc==2 or parity mismatch to a hard exit 2.

Result: one type/NULL drift in a product manifest hard-blocks all CI (blocking fast-tier gate) even with `gate_mode=warn`, directly contradicting the warn-first rollout and the "warn downgrades policy violations only" rule — this is a policy divergence, not an execution failure.
MAJOR: `core/packaging.build()` sets `out["ok"]=False` on any residency violation while `config/residency-policy.json` ships `gate_mode=warn`; warn-first is honored only in the gate, not in manifest consumers — builds fail-closed against the stated rollout plan.

AC5 conformance never runs `core.packaging.validate` (only internal `validate_residency`), has no toolchain/validator-unavailable fixture, and asserts boolean parity only — divergent error codes between the two authorities go untested.

~90 lines of new shipped validation logic landed in Python by editing the language-rule `allow` list; the full policy engine is duplicated in two languages and is already drifting (typing/null/missing-group semantics), which the language rule exists to prevent.

The gate unconditionally writes `engineering/residency-gate.json`/`.jsonl` into the working tree on every run (only tests override via env), dirtying the repo on every precheck/CI pass and risking file/store-registry gates.

Missing-group detection uses incompatible heuristics (Python: key presence; Go: zero-value combinations like `len(regions)==0 && !encrypted && freq==""`), so partially populated groups can pass one validator and fail the other → spurious parity exit 2.
MINOR: `residency_path(scope, ...)` ignores `scope`; `residency_section` strips `template`/`notes` and records no source path — audit trail of which manifest was used is lost.
`PF_RESIDENCY_PROFILES` lets Python validate against profiles different from the Go default dir; `core.packaging.validate` can silently diverge from the authority outside the gate.
AC-required tests for `language_rule_review` and precheck (45+ gates) are absent from the diff; registration exists but coverage is unverified.
`data_classes`/`subprocessors` contents are never validated (empty-string or malformed entries pass both validators) — these are the compliance-relevant fields.
`store-registry` owner for `residency-profiles/*.json` is "counsel (EDP-05)", not a resolvable module owner; owner-resolution gates may reject it.
Every gate run pays a `go run` compile inside the `fast` CI tier; a prebuilt/cached binary is warranted at scale.
NIT: `residency_conformance.json` has no trailing newline; `test_residency_conformance.py` carries a UTF-8 BOM.
JSONL rotation yields base + 3 files (4 total) while docs/registry advertise "5MB x3".
store-registry allow-list adds repo-root scratch filenames the tests no longer produce (they use tmp_path).
Inconsistent blank-line spacing between test functions in `test_packaging_residency.py`.
SUMMARY: Solid structure (Go authority, stable codes, owners, evidence trail, warn-first lever), but the two validators already diverge on JSON typing/nulls and that divergence escalates to a hard, non-warn-downgradable CI block — fix strictness parity and separate "execution failure" from "policy divergence" before merging.
Second-tier risks: Python-side policy engine duplication, build-time `ok=false` contradicting warn-first, and dirty-tree evidence writes on every gate run.

AC5 conformance is thinner than specified (no toolchain case, doesn't exercise `core.packaging.validate`, boolean-only parity), so the "identical verdict" guarantee is currently asserted more than proven.
